page: Microsoft Azure DS13-2_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs and 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. Memory capacity is substantial at 56.0 GB, yielding 28.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 115 GB of local storage, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the DS13-2_v2 sits primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng fall into the bottom 25% (weak), with scores of 1356.5 and 2688.07 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 177.59 GB/sec (weak), which drops to a poor 19.35 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Geekbench scores also reflect these limitations, with a multi-core score of 1916.0 and software compilation scoring 2540.0, both in the bottom 10%. However, the instance achieves average performance in LLM text generation using a small 135M model, reaching 90.73 tokens/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the DS13-2_v2 is its highly asymmetrical resource distribution, pairing a large 56.0 GB memory footprint with only 2 vCPUs. This makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing, allowing users to avoid paying for unneeded CPU cores just to acquire high RAM capacity. Conversely, it is poorly suited for compute-intensive tasks like ray tracing or heavy compilation. It is best utilized for in-memory caching, lightweight database operations, Redis deployments (achieving 2.83 million SET operations per second), and small-scale text generation tasks.
